news.title: Messi plushies see roaring trade as China firms get World Cup boost
news.lede: Toy charms shaped like a goat and decked out in Lionel Messi's Argentina number 10 shirt pepper a factory tabletop in China, where sellers are betting on the country's lucrative fan market for a big World Cup boost. The World Cup begins in North America on Thursday but China won't be there after failing to qualify once again, leaving their sole appearance back in 2002. Yet there's still plenty of interest in the country and the showpiece is a boon for Chinese merchants crunching out kits and accessories for fans spending on "emotional value" – a rare bright spot in a domestic economy plagued by sluggish consumption. The palm-sized soft-toy goats – homage to Messi's title as the GOAT ("greatest of all time") – are a bestseller for All Star Partner, a Chinese firm who have a contract with teams including Argentina to make branded products.

news.title: People are wrong about how they view Uruguay: Diego Forlan | Football News
news.lede: As has been seen at Leeds United, Marseille and Chile, it is not easy to succeed Marcelo Bielsa. But that’s not why, even as he spoke of 2030, Diego Forlan was not looking too far ahead. His contract after replacing Bielsa as Uruguay head coach is till March 2027. Asked why he agreed, Forlan, who has 112 caps and 36 goals for Uruguay and won the Golden Ball in the 2010 World Cup, simply said: “Well, the offer was not permanent.”

news.title: CAF Strategy Conference: Hossam Hassan – the Egyptian legend who finally took the Pharaohs into the World Cup knockouts
news.lede: Hossam Hassan will arrive at the CAF Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde having achieved something generations of Egyptian players and coaches had been unable to do – guide the Pharaohs beyond the opening stage of a FIFA World Cup. The 60-year-old took Egypt to the Round of 16 at the 2026 tournament, their deepest World Cup run, after an unbeaten group campaign and a dramatic penalty shootout victory over Australia in the Round of 32. Their journey ended in a 3-2 defeat by defending champions Argentina in Atlanta, but only after Egypt had led for much of the match and pushed one of the tournament favourites to the limit. For Hassan, the achievement carried particular significance.

news.title: Erling Haaland sues Norwegian Air over World Cup advertisement
news.lede: OSLO: Norwegian football star Erling Haaland has taken legal action against Norwegian Air Shuttle, alleging that the airline used elements of his distinctive appearance without permission in a promotional post during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The dispute centres on a social media advertisement published while Norway was competing at the tournament, marking the country's first World Cup appearance since 1998. According to Norwegian newspaper Verdens Gang (VG), Norwegian Air posted a composite image featuring one of its aircraft with a ponytail resembling Haaland's trademark hairstyle. The post carried the caption, “We’ve never looked more Norwegian”, in a reference to the national team's World Cup campaign.
